name: Fátima
tagline: Portugal's great Marian shrine, near Batalha and Tomar
summary: In 1917 three shepherd children reported visions of the Virgin Mary at Fátima, and the sanctuary is now one of the most important Catholic shrines in the world. Nearby are three World Heritage monasteries at Batalha, Alcobaça and Tomar.
seasonNote: The great pilgrimages fall on 12 and 13 May and 12 and 13 October, when hundreds of thousands arrive, many on foot. Summers are hot; winters quiet.
arrival: Buses from Lisbon take about 90 minutes; Fátima railway station is 20 km away. Lisbon and Porto airports are the closest.
gettingAround: The sanctuary and town are walkable; rent a car or take buses to the monasteries.
cashTip: Cards work widely; carry coins for candles.
foodTip: Roast suckling pig (leitão), bacalhau, and conventual sweets from the nearby monasteries.
buyTip: Rosaries, candles and religious art; Alcobaça ceramics.
baseArea: Hotels and pilgrim houses around the sanctuary

items.name: Sanctuary of Fátima
items.summary: A huge esplanade between the Basilica of Our Lady of the Rosary and the modern Basilica of the Holy Trinity.
items.expect: Free and open to all; some pilgrims cross the esplanade on their knees.
items.tip: Attend the evening rosary and candlelit procession.
